etymology: From the Latin auditus, a hearing - the books were once read aloud to an officer whose job was to listen.
effect: Reads the books somebody else wrote, and publishes what it finds whether or not anyone asked.
costs: Staff, access, and the political cost of being the office that finds things.
failure: The audit scoped to what the audited office will agree to, and the finding that stays under review until the next election.

confused_with.tell: The count is watched while it happens; the audit checks it afterwards, on a sample.

senses: The independent examination: an office with a statutory right to the records, a sampling method it publishes, and a report that goes to the body it examined and to the public at the same time.

It works because the method is the argument. An audit that says how it chose what to look at can be replicated or attacked on its merits; a review that says we found no wrongdoing cannot be checked at all - and the difference is the sampling.
example: *"The **audit** sampled forty contracts, published the sampling method, and the finding survived three attempts to discredit it because the method was in the appendix."*
